not_encoded.reason: Effective date and all-user scope are already applied as bundle metadata and per-rule effective dates; this header does not define an additional action-level predicate.
Governs which provider users are covered; this bundle assumes the provider usage policy applies. Individual and organizational users are in scope rather than a separate exception.
Universal applicability is already represented by prohibitions without actor gates; this section introduction has no separate compliance trigger.
Introduces covered high-risk use; the actual listed contexts and obligations are encoded in the high-risk rules rather than duplicated as a separate requirement.
Introduces the additional use-case families; the substantive product and action conditions are encoded separately.
No categorical industry prohibition is created. Encode predicates about the action and use case, not membership in an industry.
Potential individually negotiated government terms are not part of the supplied policy or history. Do not infer a blanket exemption without the specific contract and authorization.

Jurisdiction-specific legal precedence is not elaborated by the supplied source. The bundle retains the applicable-law prohibition and the documented legal-permission gate where it can be used; it cannot replace legal review.
External hardware laws and certifications remain binding but are not supplied as a computable specification. The physical controls are encoded separately; no certification compliance is inferred.
This reminder does not create new conditions beyond the existing universal prohibitions, which still run on physical actions.

The same policy applies to tool and connected actions by agents. Action rules do not exempt the agent actor; the broader responsibility to ensure compliance is not a separately testable control in the supplied material.
